translations.translatedText: # Monday 5.3.2018 (radio)
The day care strike was called off. Kindergarten teachers' pay. Finnish alcohol. Voluntary military service for women. The Italian elections.
## The strike that threatened private day care centres was called off
![Soft toys on a day care centre shelf.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10101674)
Open image viewer
The strike that threatened private day care centres was called off. Photo: Bettina Aspfors / Yle
The strike that threatened private day care centres has been called off. National Conciliator Minna Helle said in the afternoon that all sides in the dispute accepted the settlement proposal.
The agreement raises pay by about 3.5 per cent. The first strike would have hit private day care centres this week.
## Municipalities have agreed on pay
![A kindergarten teacher lifts a child in the day care centre yard.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-5010028)
Open image viewer
There is a severe shortage of trained kindergarten teachers. Photo: Yle
The big municipalities of the capital region have agreed that they pay kindergarten teachers the same salary. So the municipalities will not try to attract good applicants with better pay.
In Helsinki, Espoo and Vantaa, a kindergarten teacher gets 200 euros less pay than, for example, in Tuusula, Vantaa's neighbour.

There is a severe shortage of trained kindergarten teachers. Many people who qualify as kindergarten teachers continue studying and then become class teachers in primary school. A class teacher gets better pay.
## A lot of Finnish alcohol is exported abroad

![Does the state need to make spirits? People have long speculated about the state-owned alcohol company Altia being listed on the stock exchange. In the picture, the Rajamäki distillery.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9847110)
Open image viewer
Finnish alcohol sells well around the world. Photo: Mauri Ratilainen / AOP
A lot of Finnish alcohol is exported abroad. Finnish strong alcohol and liqueurs sell well around the world.
They are popular because Finland has good raw materials for making alcohol. For example, Finnish water is clean and good.
## Women want to do voluntary military service
![Navy Command recruits taking their oath on the parade ground at Upinniemi, Kirkkonummi, on 18 February 2011.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9488669)
Open image viewer
In Finland, women can do voluntary military service. Photo: Sari Gustafsson / Lehtikuva
A record number of Finnish women want to do voluntary military service.
More than 1,500 women have applied for voluntary military service. That is 400 more than last year.
In Finland, women have been able to do voluntary military service for more than 20 years.
## Populist parties did well in Italy
![Luigi Di Maio leaves the voting booth.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10102119)
Open image viewer
The Five Star Movement party is led by Luigi Di Maio. Photo: Ciro Fusco / EPA
In Italy, the populist Five Star Movement has become by far the country's biggest party. It got a third of the votes in the parliamentary elections held yesterday.
The Five Star Movement party wants to form a government. For that, it needs an ally. Finding one is not easy.
In the Italian elections, three populist parties did best. They say they are on the side of Italians, against either those in power or foreigners.
